fact: The brightest star of the northern sky's Boötes — an ageing orange giant racing through the galaxy on an unusual orbit.
bio: Arcturus (Alpha Boötis) is an orange giant just 37 light-years away. It belongs to an older population of stars moving steeply relative to the galactic disc, giving it a large proper motion.
cultural: In Hawaiian tradition Arcturus is Hōkūleʻa, the 'Star of Gladness' — the zenith star of Hawaii and a key wayfinding star for Polynesian voyagers, later lending its name to the famous voyaging canoe.
